fact_check.claim: Resident permit about $753 a year
fact_check.note: Page lists Resident $752.98 annual; map labeled 2025-26. Rounding to $753 is fine.

fact_check.claim: Resident permit prorated daily from September 1
fact_check.note: Page table says daily proration from September 1 for resident, but the Requirements section says August 16 for all annual permits; the page contradicts itself. The article states September 1 flatly.

fact_check.claim: Resident permit applies to North, South, West or Hasbrouck and is for university housing residents
fact_check.note: The fetch confirmed only that the ND (North Campus) permit is capped and limited to North Campus residents of university-owned housing; the South, West and Hasbrouck lot names were not confirmed in the retrieved content.

fact_check.claim: Resident and commuter permits are limited availability; North Campus ND permit 'extremely limited' and capped
fact_check.note: Page marks both 'LIMITED AVAILABILITY' and ND 'Extremely limited', sales capped. Permits recalled if eligibility not met.

fact_check.claim: Commuter B permit $359.77 a year
fact_check.note: Commuter (B) $359.77 annual.

fact_check.claim: Motorcycle permit $120.01
fact_check.note: Motorcycle (M) $120.01.

fact_check.claim: Permits first come, first served, space available; students must register plate even without a permit; enforced whenever the university is open; Daily Decision pay per day via ParkMobile
fact_check.note: All four points appear on the page.

fact_check.claim: Student parking page lists no first-year restriction (FAQ)
fact_check.note: Only first-year item on the page is free TCAT. A search result also showed a Cornell graduate school page discouraging first-year cars; article's wording is limited to the student parking page, so accurate as written.

fact_check.claim: TCAT OmniRide annual pass $200
fact_check.note: $200 per year, prorated monthly.

fact_check.claim: First-years get automatic unlimited rides; end Aug 31 for fall entrants, Dec 31 for spring entrants
fact_check.note: Matches, no extensions.

fact_check.claim: After first year, registered degree students ride free after 6 pm weekdays and all day weekends
fact_check.note: Matches. The page also says PhD students and graduate assistants receive free OmniRide passes, which the article omits.

fact_check.claim: Sun, Nov 2024: students without a pass lost earlier all-hours free access; Amy Hinesley, class of 2025, bought a bus pass after her swipe stopped working
fact_check.note: Hinesley quote: 'I ended up buying a bus pass after the swiping access got taken away.' Article also says drivers were told to let students ride free during free periods.

fact_check.claim: Cornell subsidizes annual Carshare memberships for undergraduate and graduate students
fact_check.note: Subsidized via the Commuter Alternative Program.

fact_check.claim: Four pickup locations on campus and four more in Collegetown and nearby neighborhoods; Carshare is the only car-sharing service named
fact_check.note: Four on campus, four in Collegetown/nearby; no other carsharing service named (Finger Lakes Rideshare is a ride board).

fact_check.claim: Just In Case: $30 a year, $9/hour plus 42 cents/mile, for under 6 hours a month
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: It's My Car: $310 a year, $6/hour plus 42 cents/mile, for over 6 hours a month
fact_check.note: Matches.

fact_check.claim: One-time $20 application fee per driver; 8% sales tax and 12% special passenger car rental tax
fact_check.note: Fee is nonrefundable and per driver per application; taxes on hourly and mileage charges.

fact_check.claim: Gas or EV charging, maintenance and insurance are included
fact_check.note: Home page: 'never pay for gas' and 'Maintenance and insurance included.'

fact_check.claim: Worked example: 3 hours and 30 miles on Just In Case = $27 + $12.60 = about $39.60 before taxes
fact_check.note: Arithmetic correct with the published rates; labeled as the article's own arithmetic.

fact_check.claim: Eligibility: 18+, full unrestricted license held at least two years; under 21 needs clean record; 18-20 need signed consent form and declarations page with at least $300,000 liability
fact_check.note: Matches; page also requires under-21 applicants to be covered by their own insurance policy, which the article omits, and the $300,000 is per accident.

fact_check.claim: KloudKoder found the two-year rule rules out most underclassmen
fact_check.note: Poster said most freshmen will not have the two years, not most underclassmen. Article overstates to all underclassmen.

fact_check.claim: blprof said North Campus pass was $750 for the year and you cannot drive to class; jfx246 said class buildings have no own lots; Ranza123 said parking is expensive with little available
fact_check.note: Paraphrases match. Ranza123 wrote 'scarce and expensive'. $750 is backed by the official $752.98.

fact_check.claim: 3rdsontocollege and blprof said buses to NYC are easy and direct
fact_check.note: 3rdsontocollege said bus services to NYC are easy and direct; blprof said buses to NYC exist because many students come from there. Slightly stronger for blprof than stated, acceptable.

fact_check.claim: OurBus will run four to six buses daily between Cornell and Manhattan, stops at Ithaca Commons, West Campus and North Campus
fact_check.note: Sun, Sept 2, 2026. Seven days a week; no fares given.

fact_check.claim: OurBus co-founder Axel Hellman said demand rose partly because Ithaca Tompkins Airport lost its direct Newark flight in 2025
fact_check.note: Hellman attributed higher ridership partly to loss of the Newark flight in 2025. Article gives no fares, as the writer says.

fact_check.claim: Insurance, gas, maintenance and registration costs for owning a car are on no Cornell page
fact_check.note: Not on the pages fetched; no hard number stated, so nothing to verify. This is a content gap, not an error.

beats_top.query: should I bring a car cornell ithaca cost
beats_top.why: The #1 result is a 2012 Ithaca College opinion piece with no current Cornell pricing, while ours gives current official Cornell permit, TCAT and Carshare prices and an answer in the first paragraph. It is still weaker than it could be because it never prices the full cost of owning a car or compares totals by scenario.
changes: Add a side-by-side annual cost comparison for a typical scenario: resident permit plus insurance, gas and maintenance versus Carshare Just In Case or TCAT, using only sourced numbers or clearly labelled own arithmetic from the published rates.
Add the PhD/graduate assistant free OmniRide pass and the Carshare under-21 own-insurance requirement so graduate and younger students get their real answer.
State clearly in the first paragraph or table that rates are 2025-26 and that 2026-27 rates should be confirmed on Cornell's page (it already says so; keep it prominent).

fixes: Replace 'prorated daily from September 1' for the resident permit with wording that reflects the source conflict: the student parking page shows September 1 in the rate table but August 16 in the Requirements section for annual permits, so tell readers to confirm the start date at purchase; source https://fcs.cornell.edu/departments/transportation-delivery-services/parking/parking-students

Remove 'North, South, West or Hasbrouck' from the resident permit table row label and use 'Resident permit' (or only the lots the page confirms), and say the ND North Campus permit is limited to North Campus residents of university-owned housing; source https://fcs.cornell.edu/departments/transportation-delivery-services/parking/parking-students

Change 'found the two-year rule rules out most underclassmen' to say KloudKoder found most freshmen will not have the two years of licensing Carshare requires; source https://talk.collegeconfidential.com/t/should-i-bring-a-car/1811430

In the TCAT paragraph add that PhD students and graduate assistants receive free OmniRide passes, with the link to https://fcs.cornell.edu/departments/transportation-delivery-services/sustainable-transportation-options/bus-services-privileges-passes

In the Carshare eligibility paragraph add that applicants under 21 must also be covered by their own insurance policy and that the $300,000 liability is per accident; source https://www.ithacacarshare.org/eligibility/

Add a short scenario cost comparison (table or list) for a student who owns a car versus uses Carshare Just In Case versus TCAT, built only from the sourced rates above (permit $752.98, Commuter B $359.77, Carshare $30 plus usage, OmniRide $200) and labeled as the article's own arithmetic. Keep insurance and gas marked as 'price these yourself' unless a sourced figure is added with a link.
